title: Check: network troubleshooting
description: Five questions on isolating a connectivity fault.

questions.prompt: curl by Service name fails; curl by ClusterIP works. What is broken?
questions.explanation: The IP path is proven. Only the name lookup is failing, which points at CoreDNS or the Pod's resolv.conf.

questions.prompt: Both the Service name and the ClusterIP fail, but the Pod IP works. What is broken?
questions.explanation: Pod IP reachability proves CNI and the container. Service VIPs are kube-proxy's job.

questions.prompt: Write a command that tests DNS from inside the cluster using a throwaway Pod.
questions.explanation: kubernetes.default is always present, so a failure there is DNS itself rather than your Service.

questions.prompt: Connectivity broke right after a NetworkPolicy was applied. What is the first suspect?

options.text: The policy isolated the Pods and does not permit the traffic you need - often DNS

questions.explanation: Policies are additive allow-lists. The moment one selects a Pod, everything not permitted is denied.

questions.prompt: A NodePort answers on one node but not another. What does that suggest?

options.text: kube-proxy is unhealthy on the failing node

questions.explanation: Every node should forward a NodePort. Per-node behaviour means a per-node component.
